summary: Assistance requested: optimizer misconfiguration caused throughput/latency degradation after quant/profile change; request recovery playbook and operator checklist
description: Issue summary: Customer reported a sharp increase in p95/p99 latency and user-facing timeouts after applying an updated quantization profile plus aggressive batching/caching recommendations. Impact: production inference failures and degraded UX for a subset of endpoints (customer's dedicated pool). Timeline: profile pushed ~2026-03-13 10:17 UTC; first alerts at 10:45 UTC. Customer requests an operator-focused recovery playbook to safely unwind optimizations and restore baseline latency without data loss or model-version drift.
impact: Elevated latencies causing request timeouts for web-facing product; approx 18% error increase and tail-latency spikes (p99 up ~2.8x). Affects a set of customer routes pinned to the updated quant profile on Dedicated cluster.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) On customer's dedicated pool, apply quant profile: quant_v2_aggressive (per customer change at 2026-03-13 10:17 UTC).
2) Enable batch_max_tokens=2048 and batch_window_ms=40 as part of optimizer config and turn on prefix KV caching for session reuse.
3) Send mixed-size chat traffic used in production (short system prompts + long user messages).
4) Observe increased queueing depth on serving runtime and p95/p99 latency regressions in the console.
logs: [2026-03-13T10:45:12Z] serving-runtime WARN queue_depth=78 p95_ms=412 p99_ms=1236 route=/api/v1/generate
[2026-03-13T10:46:03Z] optimizer ERROR quant_apply: kernel_mismatch for layer_7 -> fallback path triggered
investigation_notes: Support triage: Confirmed spike aligns with quant profile push + batch config change; no infra region-wide outage reported.

Initial hypothesis: aggressive quant profile combined with larger batch sizing created kernel selection mismatch and higher per-request memory pressure, triggering additional queuing and occasional GPU OOMs on a subset of nodes.
Telemetry: node-level OOM traces and allocator logs reference quantized-kernel codepaths; sample trace attached to PR below.
Canary behavior: rolling canary (3 nodes) showed degraded tail-latency before full rollout — suggests insufficient canary coverage or missing rollback threshold.

Risk assessment: immediate rollback of quant profile will change model execution path; must ensure KV-cache consistency and tokenization parity when switching between quantized and non-quantized variants.
comments: Customer (AtlasHealth) 2026-03-13 11:02 UTC: 'We started seeing 504s shortly after the update. We need a safe plan to get back to baseline while we investigate quality tradeoffs.'
Support (Aisha) 2026-03-13 11:15 UTC: 'Gathering config snapshots and telemetry; requesting permission to apply a staged rollback on a single canary lane.'

SRE (Diego) 2026-03-13 11:28 UTC: 'Recommend immediate mitigation: reduce batch_max_tokens to 256 and batch_window_ms to 10 on canary nodes, disable prefix KV cache for the canary, and monitor p95/p99 for 10 minutes before widening.'
Customer (AtlasHealth) 2026-03-13 11:35 UTC: 'Approved canary mitigation. Please proceed; we need clear checkpoints before full revert.'

Eng (runtime team) 2026-03-13 12:10 UTC: 'Prepared non-quant variant (fp16) with identical model artifact tag; readiness check passed. Will coordinate a canary swap once mitigation metrics stabilize.'
Support (Aisha) 2026-03-13 12:40 UTC: 'Canary metrics returned to baseline p95 within 8 minutes after mitigation. Preparing operator checklist for full recovery and post-mortem steps.'
resolution_notes: Mitigations applied (canary-first): reduced batch_max_tokens to 256, lowered batch_window_ms to 10, disabled prefix KV cache on canary nodes (3/3), swapped quantized model to fp16 non-quant variant in canary. p95/p99 returned to near-baseline within 10 minutes.

Full recovery plan executed: staged rollout of non-quant variant across dedicated pool with 5m observation windows per roll-group; batching settings held conservative during rollout. No customer data was lost; sessions maintained via cache invalidation sequence to avoid staleness.

Root cause (preliminary): quant_v2_aggressive used kernel/packing that increased temporary memory per-inference for mixed-length prompts and interacted poorly with large batch windows on this workload. This increased queuing and occasional allocation failures on nodes with slightly lower free memory (noisy neighbor exacerbation).

Permanent actions: revert customer's active routes back to fp16 non-quant model by default; create a safer quant profile (quant_v2_moderate) and recommend staged canary with a minimum 5-node canary and automated rollback threshold for p95 increase >20% or error rate >5%.
Follow-up: schedule a joint session with AtlasHealth to test the moderate quant profile against representative workloads and to tune batching policies.
follow_up_actions: 1) Add automated guardrail: block aggressive quant profile rollouts unless canary_size >= 5 and canary_window >= 15m.
2) Create a telemetry alert for kernel_mismatch and allocator_pressure to trigger auto-mitigation runbook.
3) Provide AtlasHealth with a scheduled testing window and run the quant_v2_moderate profile against a production-mirroring load generator.
4) Update console UI to surface per-route optimizer change history and one-click revert for dedicated customers with appropriate safety checks.
